summary: A 1932 Aermotor fire tower near Liberia, NC, where Bessie Haithcock was the first woman to staff a state lookout; NRHP-listed in 2000 and now a historic exhibit.

facts.design: Four-sided steel truss frame with bolted connections; glass-enclosed cab reached by an inside stairway

events.note: Built by the Aermotor Company per Wikipedia and NHLR; a 1932 state report quoted by Eastern US Lookouts gives 80 feet
Eastern US Lookouts and Wikipedia; the NHLR says active use through 1990
Added to the National Register of Historic Places March 3, 2000

corrections.why: The NHLR and Wikipedia both give about 100 feet. The record's 24.4 m (80 ft) matches only the 1932 state report figure quoted by Eastern US Lookouts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia and the NHLR give about 100 feet; the 1932 state report quoted by Eastern US Lookouts gives 80 feet. The National Register form is quoted as 100 feet with internally inconsistent measurements. We use 100 feet (30.5 m) and mention the 80-foot figure in the story.
The NHLR says active use through 1990; Wikipedia and Eastern US Lookouts say 1993. We use 1993 because two sources agree.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination PDF (npgallery GetAsset for NRIS 00000164) returned no readable text, so the 1999 Van Dolsen nomination was not read; it would settle the height and staffing dates. A Facebook post from Old Homes of North Carolina reports a 1970 sale by the Haithcock heirs to the state and a spring 1993 end of staffing, but it could not be fetched, so it is not used. No source found on current access or climbing. The 1932 state report is known only through the Eastern US Lookouts quotation.
